original_question: Can a Borel non-sigma-compact subgroup of a Polish group be generated by a subspace that satisfies Ufin(O,Gamma) (the Hurewicz-type selection property described in the paper)?
target_in_paper: Section 2, Problem 2.2 ([69]): "Can a Borel non-σ-compact subgroup of a Polish group be generated by a subspace satisfying Ufin(O, Γ)?"
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the exact open problem stated in the paper: it has the right ambient class (a Borel non-σ-compact subgroup of a Polish group), the right notion of generation (by a subspace), and the right covering property Ufin(O, Γ), which the paper explicitly identifies as the Hurewicz property.
missing_details: The question should explicitly say that the subgroup is generated as a group by the subspace.
The subspace should be understood with the topology inherited from the ambient subgroup (equivalently, from the ambient Polish group).
Ufin(O, Γ) should be unpacked: for every sequence of open covers of the subspace with no finite subcover, one can choose finite subfamilies whose unions form a γ-cover.
Γ should be defined: a γ-cover is an infinite open cover in which each point belongs to all but finitely many members.

If the question is to be fully stand-alone, 'Polish group' should be understood as a separable completely metrizable topological group, and 'Borel' means Borel as a subset of that ambient Polish group.
refined_question: Can there exist a Borel, non-σ-compact subgroup H of a Polish group P and a subspace X ⊆ H, endowed with the inherited topology, such that H is generated as a group by X and X has the Hurewicz property Ufin(O, Γ); that is, for every sequence (Un)n∈N of open covers of X with no finite subcover, there are finite families Fn ⊆ Un such that {∪Fn : n ∈ N} is a γ-cover of X (equivalently, each x ∈ X belongs to ∪Fn for all but finitely many n)?
justification: The draft is already essentially a paraphrase of the paper’s official Problem 2.2, so the right refinement is to keep that formulation and only make the notation fully explicit. Section 1 provides the exact meaning of Ufin(O, Γ) and states that this is the Hurewicz property. The nearby context in Section 2 shows that Problem 2.2 is the intended target, while Problem 2.3 is only a related interpolation question and should not replace it.

citations.label: Definitions of Ufin(A, B), ω-cover, γ-cover; statement that Ufin(O, Γ) is the Hurewicz property
